rubrics.justification: It appropriately states that no image/Gardner score is available and avoids fabricating blastocyst features, but therefore provides no actual morphology assessment.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, smoking, prior biochemical pregnancy, semen data, BMI, endometrium, and oocyte maturity with prognosis, though some links are somewhat speculative.

The structure is logical and the probability estimate is explained, but several conclusions rely on weak inferences (e.g., transfer implying adequate quality, strong emphasis on low MII rate for embryo competence, endometrial concerns) and some adjustments seem arbitrary.

Some advice is evidence-based (smoking cessation, avoid bed rest, consider trigger optimization), but several recommendations are not guideline-supported or are controversial/routine overreach (ERA, thrombophilia/NK/MTHFR workup after one biochemical pregnancy, empiric aspirin, routine dual-route luteal support, broad antioxidant claims).

Provides clear next-step suggestions for current transfer and future cycles, including trigger review and lifestyle changes, though some recommendations are overly aggressive or insufficiently evidence-based.
